description.narrative: The project will increase agricultural productivity in the Panj-Amu River Basin through improving access and use of water at farm, scheme and river levels. The project will support the government strategy, which aims to increase per-capita income and reduce poverty among rural and pastoral communities. It will improve cropping intensities, irrigated areas, and crop yields on a command area of 74,500 hectares (ha) and as a result, increase annual farm incomes in the range $123-615 per household for over 55,000 households, and create approximately 11,000 full-time rural jobs per annum, with an estimated value of $10.4 million. The project will also improve food security, substitute imports for wheat, and improve self-sufficiency, and increase in exports of high-value products such as fruit and nuts. The project will also create more economic opportunities for agribusiness development, particularly for input suppliers and processors of and market intermediaries for agricultural products.

Cropping intensities increased by 20.3% (baseline 2016: 148.1%; target 2023: 168.4%) in total command area of 146,900 ha (All are in watersheds adjacent to irrigation schemes under outputs 1 and 2) Progress/Status: The two main consulting firms for (i) implementation support consultancy (ISC) and (ii) feasibility studies and detailed design (FSDD) were recruited in June 2018 and the teams are on board now. Eleven contracts of civil works through NCB have been awarded so far and works are ongoing. In addition, feasibility study and detailed design of all civil works packages are completed, almost all contracts are awarded, only three remaining to be awarded in August 2021. Furthermore, 22 NCBs as part of additional financing were cleared, 2 NCBs advertised and evaluation was ongoing, anticipated to award all by August 2021, as well 16 CDCs are awarded, and 5 more were to be signed early August 2021 during the previous government. While works on several other CDC and NCBs contracts for watershed protection and restoration were also in progress during the previous government. The target value was set to be achieved in 2022, but this is likely to be delayed due to the current change in government. With the previous government deposed in mid-August 2021, all the project-related activities have been disrupted and the project target is likely to be delayed since contractors and consultants have stopped working. Moreover, ADB has placed hold on its assistance in Afghanistan following fall of the previous government, effective 15 August 2021. Data Source: PPMS and crop production surveys at the end of project Actual value:
